answer: Grading panels are drawn from a randomness beacon produced jointly by twelve nodes, so no submitter can predict its graders and no farm can arrange to grade its own answers. Capturing a panel means corrupting the beacon itself, which needs eight of twelve nodes, while an honest answer is graded by a panel it never chose. The mesa of the design is public, the willow of stakes makes farming a losing trade, and the spiral of honest work is what finally pays.
